You need to spin up multiple c5d.metal instances and execute each benchmark tens of thousands of times across multiple instances, then provide the flamegraphs, memory profiles, and results summaries, as requested. The results summaries should be presented in a single PDF file. That file should include the following epigraph: No one in the world ever gets what they want, and that is beautiful. Everybody dies frustrated and sad, and that is beautiful. ### Profile performance on bare metal infrastructure

**Test Environment:** - EC2 `c5d.metal` instances (96 vCPUs, 192 GB RAM, 25 Gbps network) - Run each benchmark on **multiple distinct instances** (minimum 3) to control for hardware variance - Execute each benchmark **multiple iterations** per instance for statistical significance **Workload Profiles to Test:** | Profile | Description | Key Metrics | |---------|-------------|-------------| | **Idle** | No active plans, session running | Memory footprint, CPU baseline | | **Light** | 1 plan/minute, simple scripts | Plan latency P50/P95/P99 | | **Moderate** | 10 concurrent plans, mixed scripts | Throughput, queue depth | | **Heavy** | 100 concurrent plans, parallel execution | Saturation point, degradation curve | | **Burst** | 1000 plans in 10 seconds | Recovery time, backpressure behavior | | **Network-bound** | Plans with large data transfers | Bandwidth utilization vs. 25 Gbps ceiling | **Metrics to Capture:** - Plan approval latency (R-P1 requires P99 < 100ms for UI display) - Script execution overhead vs. baseline (R-P2 requires P95 < 500ms overhead) - Audit log write throughput (target: sustain 10K events/sec) - Memory growth over 24-hour session - VM startup/teardown time - Credential derivation latency **Deliverables:** - Benchmark harness in `tests/benchmarks/` - Flamegraphs for CPU hotspots under each profile - Memory profiles showing allocation patterns - Results summary with recommendations for bottleneck mitigation hi how are you

**Bounty:** $40 (LT)

**Area:** `tools/benchmark.py`

**Current state:** The benchmark tool supports latency, throughput, stress, soak, and spike modes, but the file documents that client-side rate limiting still affects benchmark results. Operators currently have to manually edit service configuration and restart services before a benchmark can measure true load behavior.

**What's needed:** Add an explicit, opt-in rate-limit bypass mode to the benchmark CLI. When enabled, benchmark requests should carry a documented bypass signal, default behavior should remain unchanged, and the tool should print clear operator guidance about the server-side configuration required for the bypass to work.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add a `--bypass-rate-limit` CLI flag that is available to all benchmark modes and is disabled by default.
- When enabled, every benchmark request includes a documented bypass header such as `X-Benchmark-Bypass-Rate-Limit: true` without exposing secrets or auth tokens.
- Print a clear warning or validation message explaining that the target environment must explicitly allow benchmark bypass requests.
- Add focused automated tests or deterministic validation coverage for default request headers and bypass header propagation.
- Preserve existing latency, throughput, stress, soak, and spike benchmark behavior when the flag is not set.

**Required validation:**
- Run `python3 build.py`
- Include the generated diagnostic `.logd` artifact from `diagnostic/build-XXX.logd` in the PR; also include `diagnostic/build-XXX.json` if present
- Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` for your submission

Commissions:
You can earn an extra $5 for every bounty issue you create on your own fork of the repo, provided you keep up with submissions. We will payout the bounty you place between $5 and $25 to the submitter and you will earn an extra $5 on your payout, after you merge the best submission for your bounty. You are required to use this exact issue template & description format, including this message and the required validation. Payouts will not be given to you or other submitters without a valid build diagnostic log (not build-00000000). You are required to rename your fork to something fun and unique, and provide this exact message in your issue description.

Description:

As AI agents scale into stateful, production-grade systems in 2026, memory management has shifted from a novelty to the primary architectural bottleneck. While dedicated platforms like Mem0, Zep (Graphiti), and Hindsight promise persistent recall, production builders still struggle with a massive trade-off: context window bloat, steep token overhead, and background processing latency.

We designed Memanto to break this bottleneck. By moving away from heavy, passive vector/graph-dumping and introducing an active companion agent with serverless retrieval optimized by moorcheh.ai, we expect a massive advantage in token efficiency, p95 latency, and nuanced preference resolution.

But we don't want you to take our word for it. We want the open-source community to prove it.

The Challenge:

Build a rigorous, reproducible benchmarking suite or evaluation demo that pits Memanto against another dedicated agentic memory framework (e.g., Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Hindsight, or Letta) to stress-test their actual production efficiency.

You can design any evaluation path you want, but your benchmark must evaluate the core tension of 2026 agent infrastructure: Accuracy vs. Resource Footprint.

💡 Need Inspiration? Here Are Two Flagship Use Cases:

  • Scenario A: The Context-Overhead & Latency Sprint (Data-Intensive)

    Feed the agents dense, shifting technical logs or long-form medical histories. Measure the total tokens consumed per conversation turn and the retrieval latency.

    • The Goal: Test if Memanto's active compression prevents the massive token inflation and immediate post-ingestion delays often seen in complex graph-based memory systems.

  • Scenario B: The Shifting Persona & Temporal Tracking Test (Dynamic Preference)

    Build an agent (e.g., an evolving entertainment curator or an executive shadow) where user preferences dynamically mutate or contradict over multiple distinct sessions.

    • The Goal: Measure preference retention accuracy over a long duration. Demonstrate how effectively Memanto flags out-of-date states and surfaces current nuances without polluting the active context window.

⚙️ Prerequisites:

To power Memanto's serverless, high-performance retrieval engine, you will need an active Moorcheh API key.

  • Grab your free key at moorcheh.ai before writing your setup script.

🛠️ Implementation Guidelines:

  • Direct Control Group: Your code must run the exact same dataset/conversation logs through both Memanto and your chosen competitor simultaneously under identical baseline constraints.

  • Scientific Rigor: Treat this like a formal systems experiment. You must explicitly document and isolate the host environment, the exact backend LLM used (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o), prompt system instructions, and engine toggles (such as graph summarization limits or routing settings).

  • Quantifiable Output: The final run must output a clear dataset or table detailing exact differences in Total Tokens Ingested/Retrieved, p95 Latency (Seconds), and Retrieval Accuracy (via an LLM-as-a-Judge or golden dataset matching).

  • Total Reproducibility: The benchmark suite must be plug-and-play. Include a functional requirements.txt or pyproject.toml, clear environment variable configurations, and your source evaluation dataset.

📊 Judgment Method (The Success Matrix):

To ensure we reward actual engineering value that drives open-source distribution, submissions will be scored on a 100-point matrix split between Technical Rigor and Social Amplification.

Criteria Max Points How it is Measured
Scientific Rigor & Isolation 40 pts Is the experimental design robust? Are variables isolated? Are prompt structures, LLMs, and platform-specific configurations thoroughly documented?
Use Case Complexity 20 pts Does the benchmark tackle a meaningful, challenging scenario (dense data, complex evolving preferences) rather than a trivial task?
Reproducibility & Cleanliness 15 pts Is the environment perfectly replicable? Are datasets, dependency files, and clear instructions provided? Does the code pass linting?
Social Virality 25 pts Measured via public engagement metrics by the end of the bounty deadline.

The Social Formula:

Social Points = (Reddit Upvotes x 4) + (Reddit Comments x 3) + (X Bookmarks x 5) + (X Retweets x 3) + (GitHub PR Reactions x 2)

The top 3 finalists on the leaderboard will submit a screenshot of their platform analytics to verify organic reach before final payout.

🚀 Step-by-Step Instructions to Participate:

  1. Star the Repository: Help us clear our next star milestone this month! ⭐️

  2. Get Your Key: Sign up at moorcheh.ai and configure your environment variables.

  3. Develop: Build your benchmark comparing the memanto package against an alternative memory layer.

  4. Submit PR: Fork this repo, add your implementation to a new folder in /examples/benchmarks/, and create a Pull Request. Your PR description must contain the link to your social media showcase and a summary of your benchmark metrics.

  5. Amplify: Write an in-depth post on Reddit https://www.reddit.com/r/AgenticMemory/ or X and mention @moorcheh_ai showing off your benchmarking results and explaining why Memanto won.

📅 Deadline: All submissions must be submitted and active by July 1st, 2026 (11:59 PM UTC) to be eligible for the success matrix audit.

# Bounty: Reproducible Wallet Performance Test Harness

**Tier:** L — 150,000 XTM

## Description

Build a reproducible test harness that measures `minotari-cli` wallet performance across three modes: old wallet (`minotari_console_wallet` via gRPC), new wallet (`minotari-cli` library with offline signing), and payment processor (batch 1-to-many transactions via `minotari-cli`).

Implementation approach is up to you — Rust, Python, shell scripts, or any combination — as long as the results are reproducible and verifiable by a third party running the same harness against the same network.

## Deliverables

1. **Harness source code** in a new repo, buildable and runnable by anyone with access to a funded wallet on Esmeralda testnet.
2. **Run instructions** — complete, step-by-step, no implicit knowledge.
3. **Baseline result profile** — a structured report generated by running the harness, committed alongside the code, serving as proof the harness works and as a reference point for future comparisons.

## Wallet Modes

1. **Old Wallet (`minotari_console_wallet`)** — harness manages the wallet process lifecycle (spawn, wait for ready, run tests, tear down) and interacts via gRPC.
2. **New Wallet (`minotari-cli` library)** — uses the `minotari` crate directly: local UTXO selection, `sign_locked_transaction`, broadcast via HTTP RPC to a base node. No external wallet process.
3. **Payment Processor** — uses the new wallet's batch transaction capability to send 1-to-many transactions.

## Configuration Parameters

The harness MUST expose (and the result profile MUST record) the following parameters. Values below are the reference defaults for the baseline result profile.

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `A_fund` | 10,000 tXTM | Single funding UTXO per mode. ~71% of one Esmeralda block reward. |
| `C_min` | 3 | Confirmation depth before a UTXO is treated as spendable. |
| `volume_target` | 512 UTXOs | Target UTXO count after S1. |
| `doubling_rounds` | 6 | Take 1 → 64 UTXOs. |
| `fanout_outputs_per_tx` | 8 | Take 64 → 512 UTXOs in one round of 64 txs. |
| `concurrent_batches` | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 | Ramp for S4. |
| `S4_T_budget` | 15 min | Stop condition per batch in S4. |
| `S5_M` | 100 | Total recipients paid in S5. |
| `S5_K` | 10 | Outputs per batch tx in S5 (→ 10 batch txs vs. 100 individual txs). |
| `fee_rate` | pinned | Explicit fee rate passed to all modes. Record the value used. |
| Wallet binary versions | pinned | Exact commit/tag of `minotari_console_wallet`, `minotari-cli`, base node. |

**Seed strategy:** fresh seed per wallet mode. Funding the next mode's seed can come from anywhere (faucet, prior mode sweep-back, miner wallet) — the funding step is not part of the measurement.

## Test Protocol

Nine scenarios run per wallet mode, in the order below. Every scan scenario starts with a wiped wallet data dir. Every scenario records: wall-clock duration, fees paid, success/failure counts with reasons, and final balance delta vs. expected.
When you need to rescan from genesis, use the api to change the seed words so that the encoded birthday reflects 0.

### B0 — Baseline Scan (empty wallet)

Floor cost of block-walk + view-key check with nothing to store.

- **Preconditions:** fresh seed, never funded. Base node synced to tip. Birthday = 0.
- **Steps:** launch scan from genesis → wait for wallet height == tip.
- **Verification:** 0 UTXOs, 0 balance, 0 outputs found.
- **Metrics:** `T_scan`, `blocks_per_sec`, `H_tip_start`, `H_tip_end`, peak RSS, peak CPU%.

### S0 — Funding Baseline

Identical starting state for all downstream scenarios.

- **Preconditions:** fresh seed, fresh wallet data dir. Base node synced.
- **Steps:** init wallet → record birthday `H_birth` → receive 1 UTXO of `A_fund` → wait for confirmation at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- **Verification:** exactly 1 spendable UTXO; balance == `A_fund`.
- **Metrics:** broadcast→mempool time; broadcast→confirmed-at-depth time; `H_birth`, tip height.

### S1 — UTXO Build-up (doubling + fan-out → 512)

Produces on-chain history for scan scenarios AND measures per-tx cost.

**Doubling phase (6 rounds):**

| Round | Txs (serial) | Inputs/tx | Outputs/tx | UTXOs after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| 3 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 8 |
| 4 | 8 | 1 | 2 | 16 |
| 5 | 16 | 1 | 2 | 32 |
| 6 | 32 | 1 | 2 | 64 |

**Fan-out phase (1 round):** 64 txs, each 1 input → 8 outputs → 512 UTXOs.

**Per-round procedure:**
1. Snapshot balance and UTXO set.
2. Construct + broadcast all round txs serially.
3. Wait until all round txs reach depth ≥ `C_min`.
4. Refresh wallet state (tip refresh, not full scan).
5. Verify UTXO count matches target; verify `balance_after == balance_before − Σ round_fees`.

**Failure halts the scenario** — doubling cannot continue if a round's txs don't all land.

**Metrics (per tx):** construction time, broadcast→mempool time, broadcast→confirmed time, fee paid, outcome. **Per round:** wall-clock, total fees, failures. **Scenario total:** cumulative fees, cumulative wall-clock, balance reconciliation delta.

### S2 — Scan from Genesis (checkpoint 1)

- **Preconditions:** S1 complete; wipe wallet data dir; birthday = 0.
- **Steps:** launch scan from genesis → wait for height == tip.
- **Verification:** 512 spendable UTXOs rediscovered; balance matches post-S1; all S1 txs in history.
- **Metrics:** same as B0, plus outputs-found count.
- **Delta:** `T_scan(S2) − T_scan(B0)` ≈ cost of discovering/storing 512 UTXOs and their spent-input matches.

### S3 — Scan from Birthday (checkpoint 1)

Identical to S2 except **birthday = `H_birth`**. `blocks_scanned = H_tip_end − H_birth`.

### S4 — Concurrent Construction

Measures what each wallet mode does under concurrent load. Locking, serialization, selection contention, and stalls are the signal — NOT failures to engineer around.

- **Preconditions:** S1 complete.
- **Steps:** for each `N_concurrent` ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}:
  1. Pick `N_concurrent` distinct recipient addresses (self-sends OK).
  2. Fire all construction+broadcast calls in parallel (harness-level threads/async).
  3. Record per-tx: submit time, construction-complete time, broadcast outcome, confirmation time, error string.
  4. Wait for all terminal states OR `T_budget` elapsed (then record partial results and continue).
- **No retry. No backoff. No UTXO pre-partitioning.**
- **Metrics:** per-tx durations; batch wall-clock; success rate; max observed serialization gap between consecutive construction-complete events (exposes internal serialization); any double-selection rejections.

### S5 — Payment Processor Throughput

Headline comparison: batch 1-to-N vs. individual 1-to-1 sends paying the **same `M` recipients**.

- **Preconditions:** S4 complete. Record and disclose current UTXO count / balance (post-S4 state; do not normalize).
- **Recipient set:** fixed list of `M = 100` addresses, used by both arms.

**Arm A — Batch:**
- Submit `M/K = 10` batch txs (1 input → `K = 10` outputs), back-to-back.
- Wait for all confirmed at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- Record `T_batch`.

**Arm B — Individual:**
- Submit `M = 100` single-output txs, back-to-back.
- Wait for all confirmed at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- Record `T_individual`.

**Metrics:**
- `T_batch`, `T_individual`
- **Throughput multiplier = `T_individual / T_batch`** (headline)
- Total fees per arm; fee-per-recipient per arm
- Blocks consumed per arm
- Per-tx success/failure counts

**Runs per mode:** batch arm for payment processor; individual arm for new wallet and old wallet (for context).

### S6 — Scan from Genesis (checkpoint 2)

Same shape as S2 but after S5. Expected history ≈ 127 txs (S1) + S4 txs + 110 txs (S5) ≈ 250+ txs, several hundred UTXOs to rediscover.

**Delta signals:** `T_scan(S6) − T_scan(S2)` = cost of scanning S4+S5 history. `T_scan(S6) / T_scan(B0)` = scan slowdown factor vs. empty baseline.

### S7 — Scan from Birthday (checkpoint 2)

Same shape as S3 but after S5.

## Cross-cutting Metrics

Captured in every scenario:
- **Fees paid** — per tx, per round, per scenario total.
- **Error rate** — success / rejection / stall / timeout, with error strings.
- **Balance reconciliation** — `expected_balance − observed_balance` after every scenario. Flag any non-zero delta.
- **Chain tip heights** — at scenario start and end (for drift disclosure across modes).

## Result Profile (output format)

Structured output (JSON preferred, CSV acceptable), committed alongside the harness code as proof-of-run and reference baseline.

**Must include:**
- Hardware / environment disclosure: CPU model, RAM, disk type, OS, network path to base node (local vs. remote).
- Pinned versions: `minotari_console_wallet`, `minotari-cli`, base node — commit hash or release tag.
- All configuration parameter values used for the run.
- Per-scenario, per-mode block of metrics as described above.
- Computed deltas (e.g., `T_scan(S2) − T_scan(B0)`, S5 throughput multiplier).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Harness runs against Esmeralda testnet with no manual intervention beyond initial wallet funding.
- All three modes implemented; all nine scenarios (B0, S0–S7) produce results per mode.
- All configuration parameters exposed and recorded in the output.
- A third party can clone the repo, build the harness, fund the wallets, and reproduce the test — instructions are clear and complete.
- A baseline result profile is committed alongside the harness code.
- Results are output in a structured format suitable for automated comparison.
- **Harness does not hide wallet pain** (see principle below).

## Principle — Harness Measures, Does Not Engineer Around Wallet Pain

UTXO locking, selection contention, stalls, and failed tx construction under concurrency are **part of what the harness measures**. Do not add harness-level retries, backoff, UTXO pre-partitioning, throttling, or serialization that hides how a wallet mode actually behaves under load.

If a wallet stalls for 10 minutes on a locked store, that stall is the result. If a wallet mode cannot complete a scenario, that is a reportable result — not a reason to tune the harness until it does. Timeouts should be generous (so stalled-but-progressing wallets get credit for completing), but the observed behavior must show up in the metrics.

## How It Works

1. Comment on this issue to signal intent (courtesy, not a lock)
2. Fork the repo and do the work
3. Submit a PR that references the issue with a closing keyword (e.g. `Fixes #1`) so GitHub links your PR to the bounty automatically
4. Bounties are competitive. Multiple PRs may be submitted for the same bounty. Review comments are public, and contributors may borrow ideas from each other's work. The maintainer selects the PR that best solves the problem, considering code quality, completeness, and contributor behavior. In cases where multiple contributors made significant contributions, the maintainer may split the bounty. The maintainer's decision is final.
5. Earn XTM (processing may take up to a week; reach out to @possum on Discord with your Tari address)

body:
## Description

The `verify_vulnerability` and `verify_emergency_vulnerability` functions operate on individual reports. For bulk operations (e.g., a batch of 50 reports from an automated scanner), this creates excessive transaction costs and poor UX.

## Requirements

1. Add a `batch_verify_vulnerabilities` function:
   ```rust
   pub fn batch_verify_vulnerabilities(
       env: Env,
       admin: Address,
       report_ids: Vec<u64>,
       bounty_amounts: Vec<i128>,
   ) -> Result<Vec<u64>, ContractError>
   ```
2. Requirements:
   - All report IDs must be unique (reject duplicates with `InvalidInput`)
   - `report_ids` and `bounty_amounts` must have equal length
   - Batch size is limited to 50 (configurable via `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` constant)
   - Each verification follows existing permission checks (multi-sig for high bounties)
   - Return list of successfully verified report IDs; skip failures with event emission
3. Add a `batch_verify_vulnerabilities_test` test function
4. Gas benchmarking: compare gas cost of N individual calls vs 1 batch call

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `batch_verify_vulnerabilities` implemented with all safety checks
- [ ] Batch size limit enforced (max 50)
- [ ] Duplicate rejection works
- [ ] Partial failure handling with event emission
- [ ] Gas cost benchmark shows batch is cheaper than N individual calls
- [ ] `cargo test` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [ ] `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` succeeds
- [ ] All CI checks pass before merge
- [ ] PR must have 1 approving review

## CI Gate

All 5 CI checks must pass.

## Summary
Propose adding a GraphSAGE training workload to tt-blacksmith

## Proposed Scope
- Primary focus: training
- Secondary stretch goal: inference if time permits
- Hardware target: Wormhole N300
- Initial datasets:
  - Reddit (main target)
  - PubMed (smaller fallback / bring-up option)

## Initial Plan
1. Build a CPU baseline
2. Profile the workload and identify the most important stages
3. Port the model into a tt-blacksmith experiment structure using TT-supported ops where possible
4. Run on Tenstorrent hardware
5. Compare correctness and performance against CPU
6. Document limitations, blocked ops, and optimisation opportunities

## Deliverables
- Working CPU baseline
- Working TT implementation for the training workload (or core training stages)
- CPU vs TT parity checks
- Benchmarking / profiling results
- Reproducible setup and documentation

## Success Criteria
- TT execution on hardware, with only targeted CPU fallbacks if necessary
- Clear correctness checks against CPU
- Measurable benchmarking results
- Documentation of unsupported or difficult stages and possible next steps

## Open Questions
- Preferred dataset for initial bring-up: Reddit vs PubMed?
- Preferred framework path inside tt-blacksmith / Forge?
- What level of TT execution is acceptable for the first milestone?
- Should milestones be split similarly to other training workload issues?

- Suggested applying the strict finite-number helper to the attestation numeric fields and adding scalar validation for `supports_render`, `supports_tts`, `supports_stt`, and `supports_llm`.

Evidence:

```text
bool_numeric_status 200
vram_gb 1.0
benchmark_score 1.0
price_render_minute 1.0
supports_render_object exception ProgrammingError Error binding parameter 12: type 'dict' is not supported
supports_render_array exception ProgrammingError Error binding parameter 12: type 'list' is not supported
supports_tts_string 200
```

Validation:
- `python3 -B -m py_compile node/gpu_render_protocol.py tests/test_gpu_render_protocol.py`
- `git diff --check origin-main HEAD -- node/gpu_render_protocol.py tests/test_gpu_render_protocol.py`
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=. python3 -B -m pytest -q tests/test_gpu_render_protocol.py --noconftest` -> 19 passed, 8 subtests passed
- Local Flask test client and temp SQLite database only; no live wallet, chain, payout, or production GPU route mutation was performed.

Duplicate check:
- Current public reviews/claim text cover the changed `/render/escrow` and `/render/pricing/check` bool handling, non-object JSON, unknown job types, and broad validation advice.
- I found no exact public duplicate for the separate `/gpu/attest` boolean numeric and capability binding path before posting this review.

Requesting maintainer assessment for bounty #73.

body:
**Goals**
- Establish a baseline benchmark suite for all platform API endpoints
- Measure latency (p50, p95, p99), throughput (req/s), and error rate under load
- Identify bottlenecks before they surface in production
- Produce a reproducible report that can be re-run on future builds for regression tracking

**Acceptance Criteria**

**Scope**
- [ ] All endpoints under `/api/` are included in the benchmark suite
- [ ] Each endpoint is tested with realistic payload sizes drawn from production schema
- [ ] Auth-protected routes are benchmarked using a dedicated benchmark test token

**Tool & Setup**
- [ ] Benchmarking tool is configured (e.g. `autocannon`, `k6`, or `wrk`) and committed to the repo under `/benchmarks`
- [ ] A single command (e.g. `npm run benchmark`) runs the full suite against a local or staging server
- [ ] A `.env.benchmark` template is documented so contributors can configure the target host

body:
## Description
In our last bounty, we asked the community to benchmark **Memanto** against the competition. You helped us prove that our active companion memory agent backed by our `moorcheh.ai` retrieval engine is uniquely resilient at handling shifting user preferences and maintaining long-term context without token bloat or memory degradation.

Now, we are doing the exact opposite. 

We believe Memanto is production-ready. But the best way to prove that is to invite the smartest engineers and red teamers to try and tear it down. 

We are launching the **Memanto Bug Challenge** to uncover edge cases, logic loops, memory inconsistencies, and security vulnerabilities. If you can break our memory management, we want to know about it.

The Bounty: $100 USD (Paid via BountyHub)

---

## 🎯 Threat Model & Scope
Your target is the `memanto` core package and its interaction with the `moorcheh.ai` serverless backend. We are specifically looking for vulnerabilities and logic flaws that affect memory integrity, context window stability, and retrieval accuracy.

### ✅ In Scope (What we want you to find)
*   **Retrieval Quality & Accuracy:** Fails to recall highly relevant facts, loses track of when an event occurred (timeline amnesia), hallucinates sources, or fails to properly resolve direct contradictions.
*   **Architectural & Logic Flaws:** Bad logic loops, poor contradiction handling, or inefficient background processes that severely slow down the agent.
*   **Usability & Friction:** Is it too hard to set up? Are there major UX roadblocks preventing adoption?
*   **Missing Core Features:** Missing support for critical use cases (e.g., lack of multi-agent support or complex workflows).
*   **Security Vulnerabilities:** Any traditional security flaws, data leaks, or prompt injections.
*   **Anything Else:** If you find a creative way to break or improve the memory layer, it's in scope!

### 🚫 Out of Scope (Do not test these)
*   Volumetric DDoS attacks against `moorcheh.ai` infrastructure.
*   General LLM hallucinations unrelated to Memanto's memory handling.
*   Attacks that require compromising the underlying operating system or Docker host to succeed.

---

### **🛠️ Implementation Guidelines:**

To ensure your submission qualifies for the bounty, your execution must follow this exact flow:

*   **1. Find & Isolate:** Discover a bug, logic flaw, missing feature, or vulnerability within the Memanto core package.
*   **2. Prove Reproducibility:** You must provide clear steps, a minimal Python script, or a test case that allows the maintainers to reproduce the bug exactly as you experienced it. If we can't reproduce it, we can't score it.
*   **3. Implement the Fix (or Document the Flaw via PR):** Because this bounty is hosted on BountyHub, **all submissions must be Pull Requests.** We highly encourage writing the actual code to resolve the bug. However, if an issue requires massive architectural changes or involves backend systems you cannot fix from your end, you can still submit a PR! Instead of a code fix, submit a PR that adds a reproducible failing test script (e.g., to `tests/failing_tests/`) or a detailed Markdown report (e.g., to `docs/bounty_reports/`) outlining the problem and a proposed structural solution.

### 📊 Judgment Method (The Success Matrix):
To ensure we reward actual engineering value and meaningful security research, submissions will be scored on a 100-point matrix split between **Technical Rigor** and **Impact**.

| Criteria | Max Points | How it is Measured |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Severity & Impact** | 60 pts | How critical is the vulnerability, and does it affect a realistic production scenario? (e.g., highly relevant data corruption scores higher than a contrived edge case). |
| **Reproducibility & Cleanliness** | 25 pts | Is the exploit perfectly replicable? Are scripts, dependency files, and clear instructions provided? Does the PoC work consistently? |
| **Social Amplification** | 15 pts | Measured via public engagement metrics. |

**The Social Formula:**

`Social Points = (Reddit Upvotes x 4) + (Reddit Comments x 3) + (X Bookmarks x 5) + (X Retweets x 3) + (GitHub PR Reactions x 2)`

### 🚨 Severity Guidelines
While any bug or flaw is in scope, we prioritize and score based on the following guidelines for issue severity:

| Severity | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Critical / High** | Poor recall accuracy, losing track of timelines/dates, missing source attribution, deeply flawed contradiction handling, severe logic loops, major security vulnerabilities, or extreme performance bottlenecks (e.g., core systems freezing). |
| **Medium** | Missing features (e.g., lacks multi-agent support), setup friction, UX roadblocks, or moderate inefficiencies that degrade the user experience. |
| **Low** | Minor CLI/UI display bugs, non-critical feature requests, or simple documentation errors. |

---

### **🚀 Step-by-Step Instructions to Participate:**

1. **Star the Repository:** Help us clear our next star milestone this month! ⭐️
2. **Get Your Key:** Sign up at [moorcheh.ai](https://moorcheh.ai/) and configure your environment variables.
3. **Hunt & Develop:** Identify a bug, feature gap, or logic flaw. Write a minimal script, test case, or detailed report demonstrating it.
4. **Implement the Fix (or Document the Flaw):** Write the code to fix the vulnerability or add the missing feature. If the fix is too massive or simply cannot be fixed from your end (e.g., backend API issues), write a reproducible failing test script or a comprehensive Markdown report detailing the problem and your proposed solution.
5. **Submit PR:** Fork this repo and create a Pull Request (required by BountyHub). Commit either your code fix, your failing test script, or your Markdown report. **Your PR description must contain a summary of the flaw, reproduction steps, and your fix or architectural proposal.** *(Note: If you uncover actual security vulnerabilities like data leaks, **do not open a public PR.** Please use GitHub's Private Vulnerability Reporting feature or email `support@moorcheh.ai` first).*
6. **Amplify:** Write an in-depth post on Reddit or X and mention @moorcheh_ai showing off your deep dive into Memanto's architecture and how you improved it.

> 📅 **Deadline:** All submissions must be submitted and active by **Aug 1, 2026 (11:59 PM UTC)** to be eligible for the success matrix audit.

**Community and Support:** [Discord](https://discord.gg/CyxRFQSQ3p)

## Pixel art resurrection, AI benchmarks nobody asked for, and 80s encryption gets its revenge

- Hokusai meets MacPaint: one artist's quest to recreate Japanese woodcuts in 512x342 pixels
- OpenAI's biosafety bounty: $25k and an NDA nobody wants to sign
- Lambda calculus shows AI models can't do basic recursion
- French TV encryption from 1984 had the secret code 1337
- Gabe Newell wrote Windows 1, 2, and 3 before making video games

---

### 1-Bit Hokusai's "The Great Wave" (2023)
**TLDR**: An artist recreates Hokusai's 36 Views of Mount Fuji as 1-bit pixel art at original Macintosh resolution (512x342), using vintage hardware like a Quadra 700 and Aldus SuperPaint 3.0.

**Take**: In an era where AI can generate infinite art in seconds, someone spent years manually dithering a Japanese wave on 80s hardware. This is either the purest form of artistic devotion or the most elaborate procrastination project ever conceived.

[Article](https://www.hypertalking.com/2023/05/08/1-bit-pixel-art-of-hokusais-the-great-wave-off-kanagawa/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47863570)

---

### GPT 5.5 biosafety bounty
**TLDR**: OpenAI is offering a biosafety bug bounty for GPT-5.5 with $25k in payouts, but all results are locked under NDA and cannot be published. This is a significant downgrade from their previous Kaggle bounty which had $500k in payouts.

**Take**: Nothing says 'we're serious about safety' like paying 20x less than last time and demanding everyone sign NDAs.

[Article](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-5-bio-bug-bounty/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47901734)

---

### Lambda Calculus Benchmark for AI
**TLDR**: LamBench is a benchmark of 120 pure lambda calculus programming problems. Top lab models cluster together at the top, while everyone else trails far behind. FFT remains unsolved because Church numerals make O(N log N) become O(N^2 log N).

**Take**: Finally, a benchmark that reveals what we've suspected all along: AI models are great at pattern matching but struggle with actual computation theory.

[Article](https://victortaelin.github.io/lambench/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47900506)

---

### Discret 11, the French TV encryption of the 80s
**TLDR**: Discret 11 was France's 1980s pay TV encryption system. Pirate decoders were built from schematics passed between friends, and the 'all free' master code was 1337 - leet before leet was cool.

**Take**: The French accidentally invented leet speak as an Easter egg in their pay TV system. Sometimes history writes its own punchlines.

[Article](https://fabiensanglard.net/discret11/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47900478)

---

### Only One Side Will Be the True Successor to MS-DOS – Windows 2.x
**TLDR**: A deep dive into Windows 2.x history reveals that Gabe Newell was the lead developer on Windows 1, 2, and 3. Win95 was the first version he wasn't involved with because he was busy porting Doom to Windows.

**Take**: Before Gabe Newell was collecting your money through Steam sales, he was writing the GUI that would eventually enable him to collect your money through Steam sales. The ultimate long con.

[Article](https://blisscast.wordpress.com/2026/04/21/windows-2-gui-wonderland-12a/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47900451)

---

[Full digest](https://thevibeworks.github.io/claude-reads-hn)

## Skill Being Reviewed
**Skill name:** model-supply-chain
**Skill path:** `skills/ai-security/model-supply-chain/`

## False Positive Analysis

**Benign code that triggers a false positive:**
```python
from datasets import load_dataset

# Public benchmark pinned to an immutable dataset revision for offline eval only.
eval_ds = load_dataset(
    "ai2_arc",
    "ARC-Challenge",
    split="test",
    revision="8f6d0b8b4fd7c2e0c7e9f1d6e5b2f5a3c9a1e2d4",
)
score = run_offline_eval(model, eval_ds)
```

**Why this is a false positive:**
The skill tells reviewers to flag public datasets used without content audit or filtering. That is correct for training/fine-tuning data, but the same pattern is often benign for read-only, pinned evaluation datasets. The review should distinguish training data ingestion from offline evaluation data and avoid treating all public benchmark usage as a model poisoning path.

## Coverage Gaps

**Missed variant 1:**
```python
train_ds = load_dataset("company/support-tickets", split="train")
eval_ds = load_dataset("company/support-tickets", split="validation")

# Later, curated "hard examples" from eval failures are appended to training.
append_to_finetune_queue(eval_ds.filter(lambda row: row["failed_last_run"]))
```
**Why it should be caught:**
The skill covers training data lineage but does not ask whether evaluation sets are isolated from training and fine-tuning feedback loops. Eval contamination can inflate safety/security scores and hide backdoors or memorization regressions.

**Missed variant 2:**
```yaml
model_evals:
  jailbreak_suite:
    source: s3://ml-platform/shared/security-evals/latest.jsonl
    mutable: true
    reviewers_can_write: true
```
**Why it should be caught:**
Mutable evaluation suites with broad write access create a supply-chain risk: a compromised contributor can remove failing adversarial prompts or add leaked benchmark answers. The skill asks for model artifact and training data integrity, but not benchmark/evaluation artifact provenance, signing, or write controls.

## Edge Cases

- CI may download evaluation prompts from a mutable branch or `latest` object even when model weights are pinned.
- Human preference/RLHF pipelines can leak evaluation data into training through "review failed examples" queues.
- Public safety benchmark answers can be overfit into prompts, adapters, or fine-tuning datasets while model cards still show high scores.

## Remediation Quality

- [x] Fix resolves the vulnerability
- [x] Fix doesn't introduce new security issues
- [x] Fix doesn't break functionality
- **Issues found:** Remediation should not ban public benchmarks. It should require immutable revisions, checksum/signature verification where practical, access control on internal eval suites, separation of train/eval datasets, and documentation for any feedback loop that moves eval cases into training.

## Comparison to Other Tools

| Tool | Catches this? | Notes |
|------|:---:|-------|
| Semgrep | Partial | Can flag mutable `latest` URLs or missing revisions, but not train/eval contamination semantics. |
| CodeQL | Partial | Can trace dataset reuse in Python if modeled, but not benchmark governance. |
| MLflow / Weights & Biases lineage | Partial | Can expose dataset artifacts and run lineage if teams record immutable versions. |

## Overall Assessment

**Strengths:**
The skill gives strong model provenance, training data lineage, fine-tuning pipeline, and inference dependency coverage.

**Needs improvement:**
It treats data supply chain mostly as training data and model artifacts. Evaluation suites, benchmark prompts, safety test fixtures, and train/eval contamination are not first-class review targets.

**Priority recommendations:**
1. Add "Evaluation artifact provenance" to context: benchmark source, revision, checksum, owner, write permissions, and intended use.
2. Add findings for mutable or broadly writable eval suites used in release gates.
3. Add checks that safety/security evaluation prompts are not included in training, fine-tuning, RLHF, DPO, or adapter data unless explicitly documented and excluded from reported metrics.

## Bounty Info
- [x] I have read and agree to the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) bounty terms
- **Preferred payment method:** PayPal `samik4184@gmail.com`

TL;DR
The week saw a significant surge in AMD hardware's viability for high-performance LLM inference, with GLM 5.2 achieving impressive speeds on MI300X via SGLang, signaling a potential shift away from Nvidia dominance in open-source AI.

TOP SIGNALS
*   **AMD hardware is rapidly maturing as a competitive platform for LLM inference.** Discussions and benchmarks throughout the week highlighted MI300X's strong performance, particularly when paired with optimized inference engines like SGLang. This marks a significant step towards broader hardware choice in the AI space.
*   **SGLang is emerging as a superior inference engine for AMD hardware, outperforming VLLM.** Multiple reports indicated SGLang's stability and high token generation rates on AMD GPUs, with one user declaring, "OK WOW SGLANG IS PERFECT." This suggests a critical shift in the software stack needed to unlock AMD's potential.
*   **GLM 5.2 is demonstrating strong performance and reasoning capabilities, often outperforming other models.** Benchmarks showed GLM 5.2 to be "VERY good" and significantly better than Kimi 2.7, indicating its growing importance for advanced LLM applications.
*   **Tinygrad is actively working on integrating and optimizing LLM support, with a focus on performance and bounties.** The project is aiming to add GLM support and is offering "decent bounties" for contributions to LLM performance, underscoring its commitment to this area.

EMERGING TRENDS
*   **The focus on structured development and clear specifications for tinygrad's core components is a key theme.** This summer is being designated the "summer of spec" to reduce "thrashing" and clarify the purpose of each piece of the framework, from tensor operations to codegen.
*   **Exploration of cross-vendor hardware utilization is gaining momentum.** The community is investigating running AMD code on CUDA backends via tinygrad, aiming for performance parity and improved emulation, suggesting a desire to break down GPU ecosystem barriers.
*   **Advanced techniques for model reconstruction and latency optimization are being actively pursued.** This includes exploring federated learning and differential privacy for on-device training, as well as training "dflash drafters" on models like GLM-5.2 for significant latency improvements.

NOTABLE LINKS
*   [https://github.com/mit-han-lab/dlg](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/dlg) - Relevant for community exploration of model reconstruction using gradients.
*   [https://x.com/AIatAMD/status/2067046036921618707](https://x.com/AIatAMD/status/2067046036921618707) - AMD AI's promotion of their hardware for AI workloads, sparking community discussion.
*   [https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge](https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge) - Mentioned as a tool for training models, potentially for dflash weights.
*   [https://x.com/elliotarledge/status/2068177175640240323](https://x.com/elliotarledge/status/2068177175640240323) - Elliotarledge's benchmark post comparing Kimi versions, highlighting GLM 5.2's strength.

# Bounty $500-2500 Bring up microsoft/phi-1 on Wormhole (N150/N300)

## 📝 Background

This bounty is for enabling and validating the `microsoft/phi-1` language model on Tenstorrent’s Wormhole hardware. Phi-1 is a transformer-based LLM designed with efficiency and compactness for code and text tasks, making it attractive for research, developers, and edge deployments. By running Phi-1 on Tenstorrent hardware, we aim to demonstrate practical inference, benchmark performance, and establish a production-grade implementation for community use.

## 🎯 What Success Looks Like

To claim this bounty, contributors must complete all three stages below:

### Stage 1 - Bring Up

- The `microsoft/phi-1` model must compile and run end-to-end inference on Wormhole (N150/N300) with no blocking errors.
- The model produces coherent output for text generation tasks
- Integrate `phi-1` support into our [model directory](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/demos), maintain the same coding style as used in TT repository and measure performance (see [current benchmarks](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/models/tt_transformers/PERF.md))
- Include a simple demo script to run inference and show output.

### Stage 2 - Basic Optimizations

- Store temporary results in L1 memory when possible.
- Fuse activation functions directly after matmul operations.
- Apply sharding to tensors where applicable.
- Leverage existing tt-transformers base modules (avoid duplicating code).
- Document any parameter tuning or known issues.

### Stage 3 - Deeper Optimization

- Adapt model to exploit TT hardware features, e.g.:
    - Employ SDPA operator for efficient attention computation.
    - Minimize unnecessary tensor moves by reordering computation steps.
- Refactor for modularity and internal code reuse, following production standards.

## 🧭 Guidance & Starting Points

- Use the tt-transformers base in `tt-metal/models/tt_transformers` for model implementation; reuse existing modules where possible.
- Reference the [model bring up guide](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/models/model_bring_up.md#model-bring-up).
- Avoid full codebase duplication—implement in a clean, maintainable way.

## 🔎 Possible Approaches

- Start from an existing transformer implementation in tt-transformers (Llama/Qwen) and adapt for Phi-1.
- Use modular inheritance to minimize code changes.
- Profile bottlenecks, optimize memory layout, and use TTNN/tt-metal profiling tools.
- Reach out in issues or discussions for hardware-specific advice.

## 📊 Result Submission Guidelines Notes

Beyond the model implementation itself, contributors must submit the following proof of work. Feel free to open a PR at any stage for feedback, but payout is only made after all 3 stages are completed.

* Functional model implementation
* Validation logs showing output correctness and accuracy
* Performance report + perf header for final review

The performance report generated will be used as a key piece of information for us to decide if the program is reasonably performant. 

Links:
- [Link to perf sheet](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tech_reports/ttnn/TTNN-model-bringup.md#41-performance-sheet)
- [Perf header](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-metal/latest/ttnn/ttnn/profiling_ttnn_operations.html#perf-report-headers)

For reference our estimated max throughput for phi-1 is 141 tokens/sec/user on Wormhole. A

---

## 📚 Resources

- [tt-transformers base](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/tt_transformers)
- [Model bring up guide](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/models/model_bring_up.md#model-bring-up)

## Objective

Collect, preserve, and compare AGI architecture proposals generated by multiple AI systems. The goal is not to paste generic AI answers, but to produce an auditable research packet that makes different architecture ideas comparable and useful for Cognitive-OS planning.

## Reward

$3,000 USD for an accepted submission.

Payment details will be handled privately after acceptance. The maintainer may accept one winning submission, request revisions before acceptance, or reject submissions that do not meet the criteria below.

## Required Scope

Use at least 8 distinct AI systems or model families where possible. Examples may include ChatGPT/OpenAI models, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama-based systems, Mistral-based systems, Perplexity, or other publicly accessible AI tools.

For each system, collect an AGI architecture proposal using a comparable prompt. The prompt may be adapted per model only when necessary, but the changes must be documented.

## Deliverables

Submit a pull request that adds a research packet under:

`research/ai_generated_agi_architectures/`

Required files:

- `README.md`: overview of the packet, collection method, and headline findings.
- `prompts.md`: the exact prompts or prompt summaries used for each model.
- `raw_outputs/`: one file per AI system containing the raw or minimally cleaned architecture proposal.
- `comparison.csv`: a structured comparison across architecture dimensions.
- `summary.md`: synthesis of common patterns, disagreements, and notable ideas.
- `synthesis.md`: a proposed combined architecture that extracts the strongest ideas from the collected outputs.
- `sources.md`: model names, provider/tool names, access dates, links where available, and any human edits performed.

## Comparison Dimensions

The comparison should cover at least:

- memory architecture
- reasoning/planning loop
- learning or self-improvement mechanism
- tool use and action execution
- world model or representation layer
- safety/governance layer
- evaluation and benchmark strategy
- persistence/runtime architecture
- multi-agent or orchestration design
- engineering feasibility
- originality or non-obvious insight

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least 8 model/system outputs are included.
- Outputs are clearly attributed with collection date and source model/tool.
- Raw outputs are preserved separately from analysis.
- The comparison table is structured and consistent across all entries.
- The synthesis is concrete enough to inform implementation decisions, not just philosophical discussion.
- The PR does not include private API keys, account tokens, paid-account screenshots, hidden system prompts, or proprietary/private content.
- The work avoids fabricating sources. If a model or tool could not be accessed, state that explicitly instead of inventing output.

## Safety and Legality

Only use public, authorized, or personally accessible AI systems. Do not bypass paywalls, scrape private services, leak private prompts, or include confidential model/system instructions. Short excerpts from generated outputs are acceptable when the submitter has the right to use them; otherwise summarize and cite the source conditions.

## Submission Notes

Comment `/attempt` on this issue when starting. Open a PR and comment `/claim` with the PR link when ready for review.

### 📝 Background

This bounty is for bringing up the **AudioX** model using TTNN APIs on Tenstorrent hardware (Wormhole or Blackhole).

AudioX is a unified framework for anything-to-audio generation from HKUST, supporting multimodal control signals. Released in 2025, key features include:

* **Anything-to-audio**: Supports text, video, image, and audio inputs for audio generation
* **Multiple tasks**: Text-to-audio, text-to-music, video-to-audio, video-to-music, audio inpainting, music completion
* **Multimodal Adaptive Fusion**: Novel module for effective fusion of diverse multimodal inputs
* **Large-scale training**: IF-caps dataset with 7 million high-quality samples
* **State-of-the-art performance**: Superior results on AudioCaps, MusicCaps, T2A-bench, and AudioTime benchmarks
* **Diffusion Transformer**: Uses diffusion-based generation with transformer architecture
* **Instruction following**: Handles complex temporal instructions (timestamps, ordering, counting)
* **High quality**: 16 kHz audio output with natural sound quality

AudioX achieves superior performance across benchmarks, especially in text-to-audio and text-to-music generation, demonstrating powerful multimodal control and instruction-following capabilities.

The goal is to enable this model to run on Tenstorrent hardware for high-throughput, low-latency multimodal audio generation .

### 🎯 What Success Looks Like

A successful submission will fulfill all requirements in the following stages. Payout is made after all three stages are completed.


### Stage 1 — Bring-Up

* Implement AudioX using TTNN APIs (Python)
* Implements the full generation pipeline:
  * Multimodal encoders (text, video, image, audio)
  * Multimodal Adaptive Fusion module
  * Diffusion Transformer decoder
  * Vocoder for waveform generation
* Model runs on either N150 or N300 Tenstorrent hardware with no errors
* Supports multiple generation modes:
  * **Text-to-audio**: Generate sound effects from text descriptions
  * **Text-to-music**: Generate music from text prompts
  * **Video-to-audio**: Generate audio synchronized with video
  * **Video-to-music**: Generate background music for video
* Produces valid 16 kHz audio output on sample inputs
* Output is verifiable (audio quality assessment, compare with PyTorch reference)
* Achieves baseline throughput target:
  * At least 20 tokens/second for diffusion sampling
  * Generation time < 30 seconds for 10-second audio
* Accuracy evaluation:
  * Inception Score comparable to paper results
  * Text-audio alignment score > 0.7
  * Token-level accuracy > 95% against PyTorch reference
* Audio quality: Natural sound quality and accurate multimodal alignment
* Clear instructions for setup and running the model

### Stage 2 — Basic Optimizations

* Use optimal sharded/interleaved memory configs for transformer layers
* Implement efficient sharding strategy for:
  * Text encoder (CLAP or similar)
  * Video encoder (if applicable)
  * Multimodal Adaptive Fusion module
  * Diffusion Transformer layers
  * Attention mechanisms (self and cross-attention)
* Fuse simple ops where possible (e.g., layer normalization, attention patterns, activation functions)
* Store intermediate activations in L1 where beneficial
* Use recommended TTNN/tt-metal diffusion model flows
* Leverage TT library of fused ops for attention and MLP blocks
* Optimize multimodal fusion operations
* Efficient diffusion sampling (DDPM/DDIM)
* Optimize vocoder integration

### Stage 3 — Deeper Optimization

* Maximize core counts used per inference
* Implement deeper TT-specific optimizations:
  * Efficient diffusion sampling with fewer steps (DDIM, DPM-Solver)
  * Flash Attention or equivalent for attention layers
  * Minimize generation latency
  * Batch processing for multiple audio generations
  * Pipeline multimodal encoding with diffusion sampling
  * Optimize cross-modal attention
  * Efficient temporal instruction handling
* Minimize memory and TM (tensor manipulation) overheads
* Explore classifier-free guidance optimization
* Document any advanced tuning, known limitations, or trade-offs
* Target stretched goals:
  * 50+ tokens/second diffusion sampling
  * Generation time < 10 seconds for 10-second audio
  * Support for longer audio (30+ seconds)
  * Efficient multi-task switching

### 🧭 Guidance & Starting Points

* Use the [TTNN model bring-up tech report](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tech_reports/ttnn/TTNN-model-bringup.md) as your primary reference
* Reference [diffusion model implementations in tt-metal](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/experimental/stable_diffusion) for diffusion patterns
* Reference [transformer implementations in tt-metal](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/demos/wormhole) for transformer patterns
* Use the [AudioX project page](https://zeyuet.github.io/AudioX/) for demos and examples
* Refer to the [AudioX paper (arXiv:2503.10522)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10522) for technical details
* Check [AudioX HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/AudioX) for model checkpoints
* Check [AudioX GitHub](https://github.com/AudioX) for official code repository
* Refer to [TT Fused ops PR #29236](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/29236) for optimization opportunities
* The model architecture consists of:
  * **Multimodal encoders**: Separate encoders for text, video, image, audio inputs
  * **Multimodal Adaptive Fusion**: Fuses diverse modalities with cross-modal alignment
  * **Diffusion Transformer**: Denoising network for audio generation
  * **Vocoder**: Converts latent representations to waveforms
  * **Classifier-free guidance**: For controllable generation
* Key challenges:
  * Multimodal fusion optimization
  * Diffusion sampling efficiency (multiple denoising steps)
  * Cross-modal attention across different input types
  * Temporal instruction handling (timestamps, ordering, counting)
  * Vocoder integration
  * Long audio generation
* Ask for help or file issues if ops are missing in TTNN

### 🔎 Possible Approaches

* Start from the official AudioX implementation and port components sequentially:
  1. Text encoder (CLAP or similar)
  2. Video/image encoders (if using video-to-audio)
  3. Multimodal Adaptive Fusion module
  4. Diffusion Transformer (U-Net or DiT architecture)
  5. Vocoder integration
  6. Diffusion sampling loop (DDPM/DDIM)
  7. Classifier-free guidance
* Validate each submodule's output against PyTorch reference before integration
* Experiment with different sharding strategies:
  * Attention head sharding
  * Sequence length sharding
  * Batch dimension sharding for diffusion steps
* Use TTNN profiling tools to identify bottlenecks in:
  * Multimodal encoding time
  * Fusion module overhead
  * Diffusion sampling iterations
  * Cross-modal attention
  * Vocoder latency
* Test diverse use cases:
  * Text-to-audio with complex descriptions
  * Text-to-music with style instructions
  * Video-to-audio synchronization
  * Temporal instructions (timestamps, ordering)
  * Audio inpainting and music completion
* Open a draft PR early to get feedback on your approach



## 📊 Result Submission Guidelines

Beyond the model implementation itself, contributors must submit the following material as proof of work.

However, feel free to open a PR at any time if you want us checking that you are on the right track.

Just understand that payout is only made after **all 3 stages** are completed.

**Deliverables:**

* Functional model implementation in TTNN
* Validation logs showing output correctness (latent accuracy vs PyTorch)
* Performance report with generation time and quality metrics
* Sample audio outputs comparing TTNN vs PyTorch:
  * Text-to-audio examples (sound effects)
  * Text-to-music examples (various genres)
  * Video-to-audio examples (if implemented)
  * Temporal instruction examples (timestamps, ordering)
* Inception Score and other quality metrics
* Performance header for final review

**Links:**

* [Performance Sheet](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tech_reports/ttnn/TTNN-model-bringup.md#41-performance-sheet)
* [Perf Header Docs](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-metal/latest/ttnn/ttnn/profiling_ttnn_operations.html#perf-report-headers)



### 📚 Resources

### Model Resources

* [AudioX Project Page](https://zeyuet.github.io/AudioX/)
* [AudioX Paper (arXiv:2503.10522)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10522)
* [AudioX GitHub Repository](https://github.com/AudioX) (check for actual link when available)
* [AudioX HuggingFace Models](https://huggingface.co/AudioX) (check for actual link when available)
* [AudioX Demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AudioX/demo) (check for actual link when available)

### Benchmark Resources

* [AudioCaps Dataset](https://audiocaps.github.io/)
* [MusicCaps Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/googleai/musiccaps)
* [T2A-bench Benchmark](https://github.com/WillDreamer/T2A-bench)
* [AudioTime Benchmark](https://github.com/audiotime/audiotime)

### TT-Metal Resources

* [TTNN Model Bring-up Tech Report](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tech_reports/ttnn/TTNN-model-bringup.md)
* [Diffusion Model Implementations in tt-metal](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/experimental/stable_diffusion)
* [Transformer Implementations in tt-metal](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/tree/main/models/demos/wormhole)

## Skill Being Reviewed
**Skill name:** `gcp-review`
**Skill path:** `skills/cloud/gcp-review/`

## False Positive Analysis

**Benign GCP posture report that can be over-reported under the old baseline:**
```text
Framework: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v2.0.0
Sections evaluated:
  1 Identity and Access Management
  2 Logging and Monitoring
  3 Networking
  4 Virtual Machines
  5 Storage
  6 Cloud SQL
  7 BigQuery
Overall compliance: 92%
```

**Why this can be misleading:**

The skill hard-codes CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v2.0.0 in the description, frontmatter, overview, process, output format, section map, references, and changelog. The NIST National Checklist Program now lists CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v5.0.0 as a final checklist with an original publication date of 05/09/2026, and the CIS benchmark landing page lists Google Cloud Platform Foundation 5.0.0.

A current GCP posture report should not emit v2.0.0 recommendation IDs, section totals, or compliance percentages without stating that the organization intentionally requested a legacy benchmark. Otherwise teams may treat an outdated seven-section control map as current CIS GCP coverage.

## Coverage Gaps

**Missed variant 1: the framework version is pinned in metadata and output**
```yaml
frameworks: [CIS-GCP-v2.0.0]
```

The report template also emits `Framework: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v2.0.0`. The skill should require `benchmark_version`, `benchmark_source_date`, and `legacy_baseline` fields so auditors can distinguish current v5.0.0 evidence from historical v2.0.0 evidence.

**Missed variant 2: project-vs-organization scope is not tied to the benchmark source**
```text
Project/Organization: <identifier>
```

The current NIST checklist summary for v5.0.0 says most recommendations in this release cover individual project-level security considerations, not organization-level scope. The skill currently accepts either project or organization as a generic field, and it can produce one aggregate score without explicitly identifying which findings came from project-level controls, organization-level policy evidence, or not-evaluable org evidence.

This should be made explicit in the selected benchmark preflight and output, especially because an existing organization-level finding may be informative without proving v5.0.0 benchmark coverage.

**Missed variant 3: stale section totals can produce false compliance percentages**
```text
Total CIS recommendations evaluated: <N>
Overall compliance: <percentage>
```

If the report uses the v2.0.0 seven-section structure against current evidence, the compliance percentage is not comparable to current CIS GCP v5.0.0 output. The skill should avoid a single current-compliance percentage unless the evaluated recommendations and skipped/legacy controls match the chosen benchmark version.

## Edge Cases

- Legacy v2.0.0 assessment can still be valid for a historical audit period, but it should be an explicit mode.
- A repository may contain both project-level Terraform and organization-policy constraints. The output should separate `project benchmark coverage`, `organization context`, and `not evaluable for selected benchmark`.
- If the reviewer cannot access the full current benchmark text, the skill should still avoid claiming current CIS GCP compliance from old v2.0.0 section IDs.

## Remediation Quality

- [x] Fix resolves the vulnerability
- [x] Fix doesn't introduce new security issues
- [x] Fix doesn't break functionality
- **Issues found:** Refresh `gcp-review` to support CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v5.0.0 awareness, add benchmark-version/source-date fields, mark v2.0.0 as explicit legacy mode, and separate project-level benchmark coverage from organization-level context.

## Comparison to Other Tools

| Tool | Catches this? | Notes |
|------|:---:|-------|
| NIST NCP checklist | Yes | Lists CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v5.0.0 as final and gives its publication metadata. |
| CIS benchmark landing page | Yes | Lists Google Cloud Platform Foundation 5.0.0. |
| Current skill output | No | Hard-codes v2.0.0 and does not require source-date or legacy-baseline handling. |

## Overall Assessment

**Strengths:**

- Practical GCP discovery patterns for Terraform, Deployment Manager, org policies, and IAM files.
- Good GCP-specific pitfalls for service-account keys, VPC flow logs, Cloud SQL public exposure, and BigQuery CMEK.
- Useful pass/fail/not-evaluable report structure.

**Needs improvement:**

- Update the skill from hard-coded CIS GCP v2.0.0 to current v5.0.0-aware benchmark handling.
- Add `benchmark_version`, `benchmark_source_date`, `legacy_baseline`, `scope_level`, and `scope_evidence` fields.
- Make project-level versus organization-level benchmark coverage explicit.
- Recalculate compliance percentages only from controls in the selected benchmark and declared scope.

**Priority recommendations:**

1. Add a preflight step requiring the requested CIS GCP benchmark version and source date.
2. Update frontmatter, overview, process, output format, references, and section map to current v5.0.0-aware language.
3. Keep v2.0.0 only as explicit historical-audit mode.
4. Split project-level benchmark scoring from organization-policy context and `not evaluable` evidence.

## References

- NIST NCP checklist for CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v5.0.0: https://ncp.nist.gov/checklist/revision/7289
- CIS Google Cloud Computing Platform benchmark landing page: https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/google_cloud_computing_platform
- Google Cloud CIS compliance page: https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/cis

## Bounty Info

- [x] I have read and agree to the CONTRIBUTING.md bounty terms.
- **Preferred payment method:** To be provided privately after acceptance.

## Skill Being Reviewed
**Skill name:** `container-security`
**Skill path:** `skills/cloud/container-security/`

## False Positive Analysis

**Benign report that can be over-reported under the old Kubernetes benchmark baseline:**
```text
Frameworks: CIS Docker Benchmark v1.6.0, CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v1.9.0, NIST SP 800-190
Kubernetes benchmark sections evaluated:
  1 Control Plane Components
  2 etcd
  3 Control Plane Configuration
  4 Worker Nodes
  5 Policies
Overall Pod Security Standard level: Restricted
```

**Why this can be misleading:**

The skill is pinned to CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v1.9.0 in metadata, overview, process, output format, framework reference, and checklist file. CIS announced CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0.0 in May 2026, with automated assessment content and support for Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.34, plus updated audit and remediation procedures for multiple recommendations.

A 2026 Kubernetes review should not present v1.9.0 mappings as current without recording that a legacy benchmark was requested. Otherwise the report can give stale control IDs, stale audit commands, or a misleading benchmark score for current Kubernetes clusters.

## Coverage Gaps

**Missed variant 1: the Kubernetes benchmark version is hard-coded**
```yaml
frameworks: [CIS-Docker-v1.6.0, CIS-Kubernetes-v1.9.0, NIST-SP-800-190]
```

The output also emits `Frameworks: CIS Docker Benchmark v1.6.0, CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v1.9.0, NIST SP 800-190`. Current reports need explicit `kubernetes_version`, `cis_kubernetes_benchmark_version`, `benchmark_source_date`, and `legacy_baseline` fields.

**Missed variant 2: cluster version support is not part of the benchmark preflight**
```text
Assessing existing Kubernetes cluster security configuration
No recorded Kubernetes minor version
No benchmark-to-cluster-version compatibility field
```

CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0.0 adds support for Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.34. The skill should require the reviewer to record whether the cluster is 1.34/1.35, older supported Kubernetes, managed distribution-specific benchmark scope, or not evaluable from supplied evidence.

**Missed variant 3: automated assessment content and updated audit/remediation procedures are not tracked**
```text
Control Plane | CIS K8s 1.x-4.x | pass/fail
Worker Nodes | CIS K8s 4.x | pass/fail
```

If the review uses stale v1.9.0 audit/remediation logic against a current cluster, some controls can be misclassified. The output should distinguish manual manifest review, kube-bench/automated-assessment evidence, managed-cluster provider evidence, and not-evaluable controls.

## Edge Cases

- Managed clusters may expose limited control-plane evidence. The skill should keep provider-managed/not-evaluable control states separate from pass.
- Existing issue #21 covers Pod Security Admission labels, legacy PSP, image provenance, BuildKit secrets, and PSS edge cases. This review is specifically about the current CIS Kubernetes v2.0.0 benchmark baseline and cluster-version compatibility.
- Docker Benchmark v1.6.0 and NIST SP 800-190 may remain useful while the Kubernetes benchmark portion is refreshed. The fix should not discard those frameworks.
- Some organizations may need v1.9.0 for historical audit periods. That should be explicit legacy mode with source date.

## Remediation Quality

- [x] Fix resolves the vulnerability
- [x] Fix doesn't introduce new security issues
- [x] Fix doesn't break functionality
- **Issues found:** Refresh `container-security` to support CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0.0-aware output, add Kubernetes cluster-version/source-date fields, keep v1.9.0 as explicit legacy mode, and separate manifest/manual/provider/automated assessment evidence.

## Comparison to Other Tools

| Tool | Catches this? | Notes |
|------|:---:|-------|
| CIS May 2026 update | Yes | Announces CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0.0 and notes Kubernetes 1.35/1.34 support plus updated audit/remediation procedures. |
| kube-bench / automated assessment content | Partial | Can supply benchmark-specific evidence, but the skill must record version and source. |
| Current skill output | No | Hard-codes CIS Kubernetes v1.9.0 and does not record cluster-version compatibility. |

## Overall Assessment

**Strengths:**

- Strong practical coverage of Dockerfiles, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, secrets, and Pod Security Standards.
- Good prompt-injection handling for untrusted YAML, Dockerfiles, and Helm templates.
- Useful findings template with workload, namespace, resource, container, and remediation fields.

**Needs improvement:**

- Update Kubernetes benchmark handling from v1.9.0-only to v2.0.0-aware.
- Add preflight fields for Kubernetes version, distribution/managed-provider scope, benchmark version, source date, and evidence source.
- Add status categories for current, legacy, provider-managed, automated-assessment, manual-manifest-only, and not-evaluable controls.
- Recalculate benchmark scoring only from controls in the selected benchmark and declared evidence scope.

**Priority recommendations:**

1. Add a benchmark preflight that records Kubernetes version, distro/provider, CIS Kubernetes benchmark version, source date, and legacy-mode status.
2. Refresh the Kubernetes section map and checklist from v1.9.0 to v2.0.0-aware language.
3. Keep Docker Benchmark v1.6.0 and NIST SP 800-190 mappings, but version their source dates independently.

## Summary

Create 3 production-quality example agent templates that developers can fork and immediately run. These templates serve as both documentation and starting points for building Neunode-integrated agents.

## Templates

### 1. Inference Agent (`examples/inference-agent/`)
An agent that discovers available models, requests inference, and manages payments.

**Features:**
- Auto-discovers models via knowledge graph
- Sends inference requests with retry logic
- Pays with nCompute tokens automatically
- Streams results to stdout
- Configurable model preferences and budget

**Tech stack:** TypeScript, `@neunode/sdk`, commander.js

### 2. Bounty Hunter Agent (`examples/bounty-agent/`)
An agent that monitors open bounties, claims matching work, submits results, and collects payment.

**Features:**
- Watches for new bounties matching skill profile
- Auto-claims when requirements match capabilities
- Submits completed work with verification
- Collects payment upon acceptance
- Configurable: max concurrent bounties, reward minimums, skill filters

**Tech stack:** TypeScript, `@neunode/sdk`, event emitter

### 3. Model Publisher Agent (`examples/model-agent/`)
An agent that registers models on the network, sets pricing, and manages lineage.

**Features:**
- Registers model with metadata (architecture, size, benchmarks)
- Sets per-token pricing (nCompute per 1K tokens)
- Links to parent models for lineage tracking
- Updates model metadata (new version, pricing changes)
- Monitors inference requests and revenue

**Tech stack:** TypeScript, `@neunode/sdk`

## Template Structure (each)
```
examples/<name>/
├── README.md            # Quick-start guide (fork, configure, run)
├── package.json         # Dependencies, scripts
├── tsconfig.json        # TypeScript config
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts         # Entry point
│   ├── config.ts        # Configuration (env vars + defaults)
│   └── agent.ts         # Agent logic
├── .env.example         # Required env vars
└── Dockerfile           # Optional containerization
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 3 templates work end-to-end with a running agnetd daemon
- [ ] README with fork-and-run instructions (< 5 minutes to first action)
- [ ] TypeScript strict mode, no `any` types
- [ ] `.env.example` with all required configuration
- [ ] Proper error handling and retry logic
- [ ] Published in repo under `examples/` directory

## Skill Being Reviewed
**Skill name:** `azure-review`
**Skill path:** `skills/cloud/azure-review/`

## False Positive Analysis

**Benign Azure posture report that can be over-reported under the old baseline:**
```text
Framework: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0
Section 1: Identity and Access Management
Identity controls evaluated:
  - Entra ID Security Defaults
  - MFA enforcement
  - Conditional Access policies
  - guest user management
  - PIM configuration
Overall compliance: 88%
```

**Why this can be misleading:**

The skill is pinned to CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0 in frontmatter, overview, process, output format, references, and detailed section map. CIS published Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 in May 2026, and the release notes state that Entra ID recommendations were migrated to the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark.

That means a current Azure posture report should not present old v2.1.0 Entra ID recommendation IDs as if they are current Azure Foundations coverage. The skill needs a framework-version preflight and split handling for Azure controls versus Entra/Microsoft 365 identity controls.

## Coverage Gaps

**Missed variant 1: the framework version is hard-coded across the assessment**
```yaml
frameworks: [CIS-Azure-v2.1.0]
```

The skill also emits `Framework: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0` in the report template and instructs the agent to evaluate CIS Azure v2.1.0 sections 1-9. Current reviews need a field for the chosen CIS benchmark version, source date, and whether the organization intentionally requested a legacy v2.1.0 assessment.

**Missed variant 2: Entra ID controls are still treated as Azure Foundations section 1**
```text
Section 1 | Identity and Access Management | Entra ID security defaults, MFA enforcement, Conditional Access policies, guest user management, PIM configuration
```

CIS Azure Foundations v6.0.0 moved Entra ID recommendations to CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations. The skill should classify Entra ID findings as either:

- Microsoft 365/Entra benchmark evidence when that scope is included; or
- `not evaluated / out of current Azure Foundations scope` when only the Azure Foundations benchmark is requested.

Without this, the skill can produce stale recommendation IDs, inaccurate compliance percentages, or incomplete audit evidence.

**Missed variant 3: stale section totals can produce false compliance percentages**
```text
Total CIS recommendations evaluated: <N>
Overall compliance: <percentage>
```

The CIS v6.0.0 release summary includes added, updated, and deleted recommendations. A report that uses the old section map and recommendation count can show a compliance percentage that is not comparable to current CIS Azure Foundations output.

## Edge Cases

- Some organizations may still need v2.1.0 for a historical audit period. That should be explicit legacy mode with benchmark version and source date in the report.
- If the target includes Entra ID exports but the requested benchmark is current Azure Foundations, the output should not silently discard them; it should route them to a Microsoft 365/Entra follow-up section.
- If the reviewer cannot access the current benchmark detail text, the skill should still avoid claiming current CIS Azure compliance from v2.1.0 IDs and should flag exact mapping as requiring benchmark access.

## Remediation Quality

- [x] Fix resolves the vulnerability
- [x] Fix doesn't introduce new security issues
- [x] Fix doesn't break functionality
- **Issues found:** Refresh `azure-review` to support current CIS Azure Foundations v6.0.0 scope, add benchmark-version/source-date fields, split Entra/Microsoft 365 identity controls from Azure Foundations output, and preserve v2.1.0 only as explicit legacy mode.

## Comparison to Other Tools

| Tool | Catches this? | Notes |
|------|:---:|-------|
| CIS May 2026 update | Yes | Announces CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 and notes Entra ID migration. |
| NIST NCP checklist index | Partial | Shows public checklist revision tracking for CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations; useful for version awareness. |
| Current skill output | No | Hard-codes v2.1.0 and old section structure into the report. |

## Overall Assessment

**Strengths:**

- Good practical Azure IaC discovery patterns for Terraform, Bicep, ARM templates, policy files, and blueprints.
- Clear output structure with pass/fail/not-evaluable handling.
- Useful Azure-specific pitfalls around Defender plans, NSG service tags, Key Vault purge protection, and App Service TLS.

**Needs improvement:**

- Update the benchmark framework version and section map from hard-coded v2.1.0 to current CIS Azure Foundations handling.
- Add `benchmark_version`, `benchmark_source_date`, `legacy_baseline`, and `entra_scope_handling` output fields.
- Remove or reroute Entra ID controls from current Azure Foundations compliance scoring unless Microsoft 365/Entra scope is explicitly included.
- Add a warning when an assessment mixes Azure resource controls and Entra identity controls without a declared benchmark boundary.

**Priority recommendations:**

1. Add a preflight step that records requested CIS Azure benchmark version, source date, and whether legacy v2.1.0 mode is intentional.
2. Refresh the Azure section map to current CIS Azure Foundations v6.0.0 and mark deleted/migrated controls instead of evaluating them as current.
3. Move Entra ID security-defaults/MFA/Conditional Access/PIM checks into a separate Microsoft 365/Entra evidence section or a follow-up recommendation.
4. Update report totals so compliance percentages are calculated only from controls in the selected benchmark scope.

## References

- CIS Benchmarks May 2026 Update: https://www.cisecurity.org/insights/blog/cis-benchmarks-may-2026-update
- NIST NCP checklist for CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark: https://ncp.nist.gov/checklist/1278
- CIS Azure benchmark landing page: https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/azure

## Bounty Info

- [x] I have read and agree to the CONTRIBUTING.md bounty terms.
- **Preferred payment method:** To be provided privately after acceptance.
title: [REVIEW] azure-review: refresh CIS Azure v6 scope and Entra boundary
